comment: Release conditions for every exact-pinned version in package.json (dependencies, devDependencies and overrides),
plus any override added to clear an npm audit advisory. An exact pin is invisible to update-npm-deps.ps1 — that
script upgrades caret ranges and skips exact versions — so nothing would ever remind you a pin is stale. This file
is what makes that check happen: on every run the script executes each `check` and compares its trimmed stdout to
`expect`. Equal means the pin is still required; different means the condition that justified the pin has changed
and the pin should be re-examined. `check: null` means no mechanical test exists — it is reported for manual review
on every run instead of going quiet. Every exact pin must have an entry here, and every entry must name a package
that is actually present in the declared section; the script reports either mismatch. See rule G100.

@codemirror/state.why: obsidian's peerDependencies names this exact version. A second copy in the tree means two CodeMirror state instances at runtime, and the editor extensions this plugin registers would attach to the wrong one.

@codemirror/view.why: Same as @codemirror/state — obsidian peer-pins it exactly. SelectionHighlightComponent's StateField/decorations must run against Obsidian's own CodeMirror instance.

typescript.why: TypeScript 7 (tsgo) breaks this toolchain: build:compile fails in obsidian-dev-utils' check-project-types (`sys`) and type-aware lint fails in @typescript-eslint (`ModuleKind`). @typescript-eslint peer-requires >=4.8.4 <6.1.0, so 6.x is the last usable major. Hold until obsidian-dev-utils migrates.

brace-expansion.why: GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg (high, DoS via unbounded expansion) is declared with the single flat range <=5.0.7, which in plain semver also matches the newest 1.x and 2.x releases — so no release on those lines can ever satisfy it and `npm audit fix` can only offer a downgrade. Every copy must therefore be forced onto >=5.0.8, and vulnerable copies reach the tree through old minimatch majors: eslint-plugin-import and eslint-plugin-react on minimatch ^3.1.2, readdir-glob on ^5.1.0, eslint-plugin-json-schema-validator on ^8.0.0, eslint-plugin-n and glob on ^9.x. A bare caret override does NOT work here: 5.x exports a namespace (exports.expand), while minimatch 3/5 require the module itself and minimatch 8/9 default-import it, so all six of those copies throw `expand is not a function` on any brace pattern. (The earlier `^5.0.8` override recorded here was wrong on exactly that point — the copies resolve the module but fail when they expand.) The override therefore points at patches/brace-expansion-callable, a wrapper re-exporting the patched 5.x implementation in BOTH shapes: a callable default, and a named .expand for minimatch 10. The patched implementation installs under the brace-expansion-upstream alias because the override takes over the real name.
brace-expansion.manualCheck: The check tracks the oldest callable-shape consumer still in the tree. If eslint-plugin-import stops depending on minimatch ^3.x, re-derive whether ANY remaining minimatch major still imports brace-expansion as a callable default. Once every consumer uses minimatch >=10 (which reads the named .expand), the wrapper and the brace-expansion-upstream alias can be dropped for a plain caret override.
